reason: E2 and E3 establish that a continuous ordered B2 matrix limits ductility and that phase inversion via annealing improves it in Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr. However, no cited evidence addresses HfZrTiTa0.53's phase constitution, its response to heat treatment, or the specific treatment parameters proposed; E1 concerns a different alloy and only confirms brittleness under tension. Thus, the core premise that the proposed treatment will invert phases in HfZrTiTa0.53 is unsupported.
premises: Continuous ordered B2 matrix causes brittleness in two-phase RHEAs
Phase inversion from continuous B2 to discrete B2 in BCC matrix improves ductility
Phase inversion is achievable via controlled annealing in Al-containing RHEAs
HfZrTiTa0.53 contains a continuous brittle ordered phase that can be inverted
The proposed 1400°C/20min + 600°C/120h treatment will induce phase inversion in HfZrTiTa0.53
